 KTR urges public to give Congress government a ‘holiday’ over promises 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 29 October 2026, 8:12 pm 
 3 min read
 29 Oct 2026 
 ANI Photo | KTR urges public to give Congress government a ‘holiday’ over promises 
 KT Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), called on the public to grant the Congress government a “holiday” in response to what he described as its failure to deliver on 420 promises and six guarantees. Speaking on October 29, he accused the administration of neglecting farmers and allowing power shortages and delays in employee benefits across Telangana.
 KTR highlighted the plight of farmers who, amid drought conditions, were forced to rely on generators and water tankers to protect their crops. He demanded the immediate release of outstanding Rythu Bandhu funds, the completion of irrigation projects, improved electricity supply, and relief measures for drought-affected farmers.

 He also criticised delays in pension payments, unemployment allowances, Rythu Bima benefits, Pay Revision Commission (PRC) recommendations, and retirement benefits for government employees. Questioning government priorities, KTR called for the proposed Rs 1.5-lakh-crore Musi beautification project to be halted, with those funds redirected to public welfare and farmer assistance.
 KTR alleged the Musi project was proceeding without a publicly available Detailed Project Report (DPR) and adequate public consultation, accusing officials of suppressing the views of affected residents and public representatives during hearings. He claimed that BRS was the sole political party advocating for those impacted and criticised the proposed involvement of the Asian Development Bank in funding the project.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Regarding irrigation developments, KTR voiced concerns about the Medigadda Barrage, citing the government’s failure to thoroughly investigate reported damage to its pillars. He contrasted Telangana’s situation with that of neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, saying that despite rainfall deficiencies, Andhra Pradesh had implemented measures to support farmers.
 On the energy front, KTR condemned frequent power cuts affecting industries, warning that electricity shortages would hamper the state’s industrial growth and deter investment. He accused Telangana of becoming an “ATM for Rahul Gandhi” and questioned the silence of Congress leadership amid the state’s drought, agricultural distress, and administrative challenges.
 Describing the upcoming Global Summit as a “Goebbels Summit,” KTR alleged excessive government spending on publicity while farmers struggled with water shortages and industries faced power outages. He noted that the previous BRS government had attracted investments worth several lakh crores of rupees over a decade without hosting such summits.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 KTR called for the publication of a white paper detailing the Congress government’s foreign visits over the past three years, memorandums of understanding signed, investments secured, and jobs created. He also referenced an alleged loss of approximately 7,000 IT jobs, stating that employment had decreased from 946,000 jobs when the BRS left office.
 In conclusion, KTR urged the government to abandon the Musi beautification project, release pending welfare funds, complete irrigation projects, ensure uninterrupted power supply, and prioritise the needs of farmers and the public over promotional activities.
